description.text: Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated (“RGA”) is an insurance holding company that was formed on December 31, 1992. The consolidated financial statements herein include the assets, liabilities, and results of operations of RGA and its subsidiaries, all of which are wholly owned. The terms “Company”, “we”, “us” and “our” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refer to RGA and its subsidiaries. The Company is a leading global provider of traditional life and health, and asset-intensive reinsurance, with operations in the U.S., Latin America, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. Reinsurance is an arrangement under which an insurance company, the “reinsurer,” agrees to indemnify another insurance company, the “ceding company,” for all or a portion of the insurance and/or investment risks underwritten by the ceding company. Reinsurance is designed to: i.reduce the net amount at risk on individual risks, thereby enabling the ceding company to increase the volume of business it can underwrite, as well as increase the maximum risk it can underwrite on a single risk; ii.enhance the ceding company’s financial strength and surplus position; iii.stabilize operating results by leveling fluctuations in the ceding company’s loss experience; and iv.assist the ceding company in meeting applicable regulatory requirements. The Company has the following geographic-based and business-based operational segments: •U.S. and Latin America;

about.description_short: Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated (NYSE: RGA) is a global industry leader specializing in life and health reinsurance and financial solutions that help clients effectively manage risk and optimize capital. Founded in 1973, RGA is one of the world's largest and most respected reinsurers and remains guided by a powerful purpose: to make financial protection accessible to all. As a global capabilities and solutions leader, RGA empowers partners through bold innovation, relentless execution, and dedicated client focus - all directed toward creating sustainable long-term value. RGA has approximately $4.3 trillion of life reinsurance in force and total assets of $167.1 billion as of June 30, 2026. To learn more about RGA and its businesses, please visit rgare.com or follow RGA on LinkedIn and Facebook. Investors can learn more at investor.rgare.com.

analysis_md:
# RGA — Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated
v5 run (engine 5.4.0), 2026-10-16. Price $266.69 (nasdaq_quote_api, dcf_numbers.json). Engine market-cap estimate $17,814,892,000 — in scope under $40B. Sector: Finance / Life & Health Reinsurance (Insurance).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
St. Louis-based global life and health reinsurer — the leading pure-play in a concentrated oligopoly alongside Munich Re, Swiss Re and Hannover Re. Segments: U.S. and Latin America, Canada, EMEA and Asia Pacific traditional life/health reinsurance, plus Financial Solutions (asset-intensive in-force blocks, longevity, pension risk transfer). AM Best affirmed A+ financial strength with a stable outlook (search result). Latest quarter Q2 2026 (release via Business Wire, search results): net income $462,000,000 ($7.01 diluted), adjusted operating income $586,000,000 ($8.89 diluted) vs $315,000,000 a year earlier, consolidated net premiums $4.5 billion up 7.7% year over year, total revenue $6.6 billion up 18.5%, trailing-twelve-month adjusted operating ROE 17.4% (18.4% excluding notable items); management cited modestly favorable claims experience and the July 2025 Equitable in-force block contributing. Q1 2026: net income $330,000,000, adjusted operating income $462,000,000, adjusted operating ROE 15.2% TTM.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $4,091,000,000; capex $30,000,000 — by override, see OVERRIDE below; SBC $42,000,000 (tag AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense — always a real cost); net income $1,182,000,000; revenue $23,698,000,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $4,019,000,000 = $60.16467065868263/share latest FY** (dcf_numbers.json base_oe_total_latest_fy / base_oe_latest_per_share, with the capex override applied).
- Maintenance version FY2025 (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, from financials_history.csv): $1,225,000,000 — far below the conservative figure, which is itself the warning for this name (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE below).
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (dcf_numbers.json). OE/share history is violently lumpy: FY2021 $60.14641288433382, FY2022 $18.80354505169867, FY2023 $59.582712369597616, FY2024 $139.1629297458894 (zero-filled capex, financials_history.csv), FY2025 $60.61377245508982 zero-filled / $60.16467065868263 with the override.
- **Engine normalized base: $60.16467065868263/share, median of the last 3 FY OE/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share in the preliminary run) — reported, but NOT used as the final base, for the STALE_FY reason below.
- Balance sheet (folded in explicitly): net debt $1,542,000,000 per dcf_numbers.json (basis TOTAL:LongTermDebt; diagnostics net debt 0.5262635351059538× normalized OE). For a reinsurer this engine figure is a holding-company sliver only — the real balance sheet is the investment portfolio ($127,604,000,000 total investments at Q3 2025 per search-result filing extract) against future policy benefits and interest-sensitive contract liabilities, and the risk is reserve, credit and asset-mark risk, not the corporate debt load. That risk is handled via the sector confidence cap and the tier softening, not a net-debt adjustment.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $4,091,000,000 − prior YTD −$2,249,000,000 + current YTD −$3,357,000,000 = **TTM $2,983,000,000** (both H1 periods are cash-negative; the TTM figure is what the legs give)
- Capex: **TTM $30,000,000.0**, all three legs filled by the override, prorated by days (FY leg $30,000,000.0 over 365 days; both YTD legs $14,876,712.328767123 over 181 days; they cancel in the TTM math) — see OVERRIDE
- SBC: FY $42,000,000 − prior YTD $25,000,000 + current YTD $41,000,000 = **TTM $58,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **66,000,000**
- **TTM OE total $2,895,000,000.0 → base OE/share $43.86363636363637** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The TTM base is the conservative choice of the two: it is below the $60.16467065868263 normalized median, it uses the most current filing legs, and it already reflects the weaker H1 2026 operating cash flow. It is still an OCF-based figure for an insurer — see the float caveat in Thoughts, which is why the tier is softened even on this base.

## OVERRIDE — capex (estimate, bounded authority)

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate, real but not wide
Justification: a concentrated life/health reinsurance oligopoly where RGA is the leading pure-play, built on decades of biometric data, underwriting expertise, A+ rated balance-sheet capacity and long-duration in-force treaties that switch slowly — against no structural pricing power over mortality/longevity outcomes, capacity competition on large asset-intensive blocks including from PE-backed rivals, structural earnings volatility from biometric shocks and remeasurements, and capital/ratings constraints.
- FOR: concentrated global life/health reinsurance oligopoly — few scaled rivals (Munich Re, Swiss Re, Hannover Re) and high balance-sheet/rating barriers to entry; decades of proprietary biometric data and underwriting expertise — the core input for pricing mortality/longevity risk cannot be bought quickly; long-duration in-force treaties and embedded client relationships — reinsurance programs renew with incumbents and switch slowly; diversified global platform (U.S./LatAm, Canada, EMEA, Asia Pacific plus financial solutions) — regional and product diversification dampens any single mortality pool.
- AGAINST: no pricing power over biometric outcomes — mortality/longevity experience and assumption updates drive earnings, not RGA's price list; large asset-intensive blocks are capacity-competed, including by private-equity-backed reinsurers with cheaper asset origination; earnings volatility is structural — COVID-era mortality, remeasurement gains/losses and investment marks swing GAAP results year to year; capital and ratings hostage — growth is capped by insurance capital rules and the need to defend the A+ financial strength rating.
- **Returns evidence (per the spec's ROIC requirement):** fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy series and no gross margin for this filer (operating_income and gross_profit are null for an insurer — those concepts are not filed), so the return lens is ROE. GAAP ROE in fundamentals.json: FY2021 0.1430317848410758, FY2022 0.07301228640022596, FY2023 0.09932826781191499, FY2024 0.06629068047337278, FY2025 0.08780922665478047 — mid-to-high single digits on AOCI-swollen equity (book value per share $201.5119760479042 at FY2025). The company's adjusted operating ROE ran 15.2% TTM at Q1 2026 and 17.4% TTM at Q2 2026 (18.4% excluding notable items) per its releases — above a plausible cost of capital, but earned in a risk business whose bad years are set by claims experience. That supports 6/10, not 7+: the measured GAAP history does not show durable through-cycle returns well above the cost of capital.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## My thoughts / overlay
- **Method range is the headline, as with APP and PFG:** on the median-of-3-FY base the same inputs printed tier S (weighted IRR 30.959579312335983%, IV@15% $663.0112342364839 in the preliminary final-form run) because the median year is FY2025's $60.16467065868263 and FY2024's spike sits in the window; on the TTM base actually used, tier A by numbers (23.916478746749326%); on any earnings-based lens (FY2025 net income $1,182,000,000, maintenance OE $1,225,000,000) the name screens lower still. The defensible range is therefore B-or-lower on earnings lenses to A on the TTM cash-flow base, with the S print resting entirely on the rejected-for-an-insurer median-OCF definition; the verdict is sized to the conservative end, B — the same one-notch insurer-float softening applied to PFG/HIG/ACGL/WRB, here applied to the A.
- **Insurer caveat on this base (the controlling judgment in this file):** for a life reinsurer, OCF runs structurally above net income because premiums are collected in cash while reserve builds for assumed blocks are charged to earnings unpaid, and OCF carries float that belongs to future policyholders. That makes even the TTM OE/share base ($43.86363636363637) an upper bound on distributable earnings, not earning power — GAAP diluted EPS and adjusted operating EPS run at a per-share level far below this base (Q2 2026 adjusted operating income was $8.89 per diluted share for the quarter, per the company's release). The engine's numbers are therefore treated as an upper-bound method, and the final tier is softened one notch rather than the base being re-pinned by hand.
- Quality is not the debate: OE positive in all of the last 5 fiscal years on the conservative definition, a leading pure-play franchise in a concentrated oligopoly, adjusted operating ROE of 17.4% TTM, a dividend raised 5.4% for Q3 2026 and $50,000,000 of Q2 buybacks (company release, search results). The debate is the entry multiple for a biometric-risk business whose cash conversion is dominated by block timing.
- Red flags to monitor: mortality/longevity assumption updates at the annual review, credit losses in a $100B-plus investment portfolio in a downturn, the pace and pricing of asset-intensive block deals (each one mechanically inflates OCF and OE), PE-backed reinsurance capacity competing spreads down, and H1-style negative operating cash flow persisting into full years.
- **Hurdle math:** on the engine's numbers the stock clears a 15% IRR at $483.37476737035706 (the weighted IV@15%) and trades 81.24967841702242% below that figure at $266.69 — but that clearing price inherits the float-inflated base, so it overstates the true margin of safety; a margin-of-safety buy price would need to sit materially below the weighted IV@15%, in words, and no hand-computed figure is quoted for it. It clears 20% at $333.64459420690486 and does not clear 25% (IV@25% $252.46029561250825 is below the price). On the conservative (final-tier B) reading, the honest claim is "clears 15% with room on engine numbers, sized like a B", not "81% upside".
